questions.question: While selling an item, a businessman allows a 40% discount on the marked price and incurs a loss of 30%. If the item is sold at the marked price, profit will be _______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount Percentage = 40%

Loss Percentage = 30%

**Concept Used:**

Cost Price = (100)/(100-Loss\%)times SP

Profit % = (Profit)/(CP)times 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the marked price be Rs 100

⇒ Selling price = 100 – 40% of 100

⇒ Selling price = 100-(40)/(100)times 100=100-40=60 Rs

⇒ Loss percentage = 30%

⇒ So, Cost price = (100)/(100-30)times 60

⇒ Cost price = (100)/(70)times 60=(600)/(7) Rs

⇒ If item is sold at marked price, then

⇒ Profit Percentage = (100-frac{600)/(7)}{(600)/(7)}times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = (frac{700-600)/(7)}{(600)/(7)}times 100=(100)/(600)times 100=(100)/(6)=16(2)/(3) %

**Hence, the profit percentage made by selling an item at marked price is 16(2)/(3)\%**.

questions.question: If P(x) = (x³ - 8)(x + 1) and Q(x) = (x³ + 1)(x - 2) the LCM of P(x) and Q(x) is:
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)

**Calculations:**

P(x) = (x3 - 8)(x + 1) 

⇒ P(x) = (x - 2)(x² + 2x + 4)(x + 1) 

 Q(x) = (x3 + 1)(x - 2)

⇒ Q(x) = (x + 1)(x² - x + 1(x - 2)

Now, The LCM of P(x) and Q(x) is

(x + 1)(x - 2)(x2 + 2x + 4)(x2 - x + 1)

**Hence, The Required value is (x + 1)(x - 2)(x2 + 2x + 4)(x2 - x + 1).**

questions.question:
ABCD is a square of side 21 cm. A circle is inscribed in the square, which touches the sides of the square at P, Q, R and S as shown below in the figure. What is the area (in cm²) of the non-shaded region? [Figure is not drawn to scale.] (Take π = (22)/(7))

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8ce27079478ec2467fe439a23ab07b186ff3d4e33ef726a8a91a90a7fa4f12f.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ABCD is a square of side 21 cm. A circle is inscribed in the square, which touches the sides of the square at P, Q, R and S.

**Formula used:**
Area of a square = a² , where 'a' is the length of each side

Area of a circle = πr², where 'r' is the radius.

**Calculation:**

Area of the square = 21 × 21 = 441 cm²

The radius of the circle = (21)/(2) = 10.5 cm

Area of the circle = (22)/(7)times 10.5² = 346.5 cm²

Area of the non-shaded region** = ****Area of the square - Area of the circle**

**∴ The area of the non-shaded region is 441 - 346.5 = 94.5 cm²**

questions.question: The area of two similar triangles XYZ and ABC are 361 cm² and 225 cm², respectively. If the longest side of the larger ∆XYZ be 38 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the longest side of the smaller ∆ABC?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∆XYZ and ∆ ABC are similar triangles

Area of ∆XYZ = 361 cm²

Area of ∆ ABC = 225 cm² 

**Concept used:**

If two triangles are similar, then the ratio of their areas is equal to the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides.

**Calculations:**

Let the longest side of ∆ ABC be x cm.

According to the question,

The ∆XYZ and ∆ABC are similar, 

Thus we have, (area(∆XYZ))/(area(∆ABC))= ((longest side of ∆XYZ)²)/((longest side of ∆ABC)²)

⇒ (361)/(225) = (38²)/(x²)

⇒ x² = (38² × 225)/(361)

⇒ x² = 900

⇒ x = √900 = 30

**Hence, The length of the longest side of ∆ABC is 30 cm.**

An athlete crosses a distance of 3600 m in 12 minutes. What is his speed (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 3600 m

Time = 12 minutes

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ We know that 1 km = 1000 m

⇒ 3600 m = (3600)/(1000)=3.6km

⇒ 1 hour = 60 minutes

⇒ So, 12 minutes = (12)/(60)=0.2 hrs

⇒ Speed of an athlete = (3.6)/(0.2)=18 km/h

**Hence, the speed of an athlete is 18 km/h.**

questions.question: The base of a hemispherical bowl has a circumference of 132 cm. Find the capacity of the bowl. (use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Circumference of the base of a hemispherical bowl = 132 cm

**Concept Used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2)/(3)pi r³

Circumference of the base of the hemisphere = 2pi r

**Calculation:**

⇒ Circumference of the base of hemisphere = 2pi r=132

⇒ 2times (22)/(7)times r = 132

⇒ r=(132times 7)/(44)=21 cm

⇒ So, the capacity of hemispherical bowl = (2)/(3)times (22)/(7)times 21times 21times 21

⇒ Capacity of hemispherical bowl = 44times 21times 21 = 19404 cm³

**Hence, the capacity of the bowl is 19404 cm³.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells rice at cost price but uses a faulty weighing machine and thus gains a profit of 25%. Find how many grams rice he is giving in 1 kg ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit Percentage = 25%

**Concept Used:**

Gain Percentage = (SP-CP)/(CP)times 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the cost price of 1 kg rice be Rs 100

⇒ Let the false weight used by the shopkeeper for 1 kg be x grams.

⇒ When false weight is used,

⇒ Selling Price = Cost Price = Rs 100 and Profit = 25%

⇒ Cost price for 1000 grams rice = Rs 100

⇒ So, the Cost price for 1 gram of rice = (100)/(1000)=(1)/(10) Rs

⇒ For x grams, Cost Price of rice = (x)/(10) Rs

Putting the values in the formula,

⇒ (SP-CP)/(CP)times 100=25

⇒ SP – CP = 0.25CP

⇒ SP = 1.25CP = 1.25times (x)/(10)

⇒ x = (100times 10)/(1.25)=800 grams.

⇒ Therefore, the amount of rice given in 1 kg = 800 grams

**∴ The amount of rice given in 1 kg measurement is 800 grams.**
